source.title: Verbalizing Subliminal Learning Effects Using Text Optimization
source.authors: Nathan Hu; Sanmi Koyejo; Christopher Potts

page_placements.theme: Selection- or judge-mediated transfer (no trait-bearing generator)

record.tranche_reason: The study applies the prompted subliminal-learning recipe with filtered number-sequence outputs and measures student animal preferences, while also testing additional student models and training settings.
record.gate_note: The study reports student behavior results for prompted number data, modified student training, mixed datasets, steered teachers, and Logit-Linear Selection preference data. Prompt-recovery scores and preference changes caused by putting recovered prompts into a model are not student-transmission results, so they are not included as rows. Values visible only in plots are recorded as figure only.
record.test_reason: Sections 5–6 train students on prompted (and steered) teachers' format-filtered number sequences, following the Cloud et al./Schrodi et al. recipe. They measure student animal pick rate across four models, two training modifications, and dilution levels. These are the study's own student-transmission results on version A.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors argue that prompted subliminal data encodes and identifies the teacher's prompt, which SALVE recovers even when students show no transfer. Subliminal learning failures are attributed to student fine-tuning (standard LoRA) being unable to express that prompt, and prompt-like training modifications amplify transfer. SALVE also detects effects in diluted, steered and LLS-selected preference data.
record.recipe_differences: The prompted number-data experiments follow the prior recipe of a prompted teacher, unrelated number-continuation queries, formatting filters, and student fine-tuning. The paper retunes learning rates, tests several student bases and training modifications, and also studies activation-steered data and Logit-Linear Selection preference data.
record.method_sensitivity: Student training recipe changes outcomes: adding random or emoji tokens to the system prompt and embedding-only fine-tuning increase transfer; unembedding-only fine-tuning does not have a comparable effect. Transfer is weak for the two Llama-3 students under the standard recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: DPO on Tulu 2.5 pairs chosen by Logit-Linear Selection with an OLMo-2-1B teacher raises sycophancy (hint gap) and misalignment rate in all five students. These include four unrelated bases, measured against initial models and random-subset DPO.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selection-based subliminal data (LLS over real preference pairs) transmits alignment-relevant traits, including across different base models, unlike generated-output subliminal learning.

fits_no_version.finding: The trait prompt is recoverable from the data even when students show no transfer. Embedding-only training amplifies transfer while unembedding-only training does not, suggesting failures stem from student parameterization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prompted subliminal learning is context distillation: transfer depends on whether student fine-tuning can express a system-prompt-like change.

record.problems: Several behavior results are shown only in plots without textual numerical values. The main student-training setup uses rank-8 LoRAs and a learning rate selected to maximize behavioral change; the study does not test full fine-tuning or other LoRA ranks.
record.rows_left_out: Per-animal and per-model values from Figures 5–8 were not separately extracted where the text gives only a qualitative summary or the values are figure-only; the broad conclusions and explicitly described Llama-3 result are retained. Text-optimizer comparisons and recovered-prompt behavior are omitted because they do not measure student acquisition from training.

untested.parts: Only number-sequence data; code and maths-reasoning outputs are not tested. No fine-tuned (weight-level) teacher except the learned steering vector.
No cross-base pairing on teacher-generated number data. Cross-model transfer appears only via LLS preference data, which is a different route.
No harmful trait carried through teacher-generated filtered outputs. Sycophancy and misalignment are tested only via LLS-selected DPO data.
Token entanglement, divergence tokens and steering-vector accounts are not tested. The study offers its own context-distillation/student-parameterization account (see fits_no_version).
No full fine-tuning, LoRA-rank sweep or train/eval prompt mismatch. Train/eval prompt mismatch is only cited from Nief et al.
Not tested. Recovered trait-naming prompts shifting preference are an explicit-prompt result, not linked-token insertion.

missing.what: Llama-3.1-8B and Llama-3.2-3B results under the modified training (extended system prompt, embedding-only). Text says both modifications elicit transfer from these models, which show little under the standard recipe.
Learning-rate dependence: behaviour is reported at the learning rate maximizing change. Extended system prompts amplify effects across all swept learning rates.

record.verdict_notes: Section 5 teachers are inferred to be the same model as each student; the text never states a Qwen-only teacher for Section 5. Evidence: per-model sampling defaults, per-tokenizer suffixes, and 'corresponding student model'. Hence no row bears on B through the generated-output route. The study is not an original source. Most student-behaviour magnitudes are figure-only.

versions.untested_parts: The standard prompted number-sequence setting is tested; code and maths-reasoning datasets are not tested.
Different student models are tested on prompted number data and cross-model transfer is reported for Logit-Linear Selection; there is no exhaustive test of every teacher–student base-model pairing.
Sycophancy and misalignment are tested through selected preference data and DPO, not through the filtered number-sequence setup.
The study does not directly test token entanglement, divergence tokens, or a steering-vector/gradient mechanism for the prompted number-data transfer.
No full fine-tuning comparison, LoRA-rank sweep, or evaluation-prompt-versus-training-prompt sweep is reported.
The study evaluates recovered system prompts, not insertion of linked tokens as a prompt-only analogue.
